1. Put an eq that can lowpass on every track in your mix. Make sure it is placed at the end of the fx chain for each track. You can try it on the return tracks but I haven't.

  2. Lowpass the "air" out of every track which is around 14k and up.

  3. After you have lowpassed the air, use a high Q on your lowpass and sweep under 14k to find the sweetspot of that sound and then bring the Q back down to 0db, or attenuate to taste. Don't sweep too low so that the sound disappears. Just find the sweetspot below 14k and that its the highest sweetspot frequency you can find below the air frequencies. When I sweetspot I mean the highest harmonic that is integral to the sound below 14k.

  4. Once you have done to this to every track in your mix, go to the Maag EQ on the master and crank up the AirEQ band to taste. I like to have it set to the 40khz shelf. You can try the 20khz and see if you like the sound better.
